title_en: Journey to the West 31: The Chain Cave
source_file: 连环画《西游记31：连环洞》（6-10岁）.pdf
full_text_zh:
[P1] 连环洞
《西游记》之三十一
原著 吴承恩
改编 陈平夫
绘画 轩观潮
河北美术出版社

[P2] 内容提要
这本画册是根据古典文学名著《西游记》第八十五回——
八十六回编绘的。
故事叙述唐僧师徒在西行取经的路上，经过隐雾山连
环洞时，唐僧被洞中的妖魔劫去。悟空施展神威，除去妖
邪艾叶花皮豹子精，救出了师父和樵夫，使隐雾山一带的
百姓又过上了太平日子。

1 唐僧师徒四人，离了陷空山继续西行，不多日，又
见高山阻路。到了山脚下，忽然狂风卷尘，瘴雾遮天，唐
僧勒马叫道：“这山里有凶气，我怎么满身麻木，心惊肉跳
呀！”

[P3] 2 悟空笑道：‘师父是被妖怪吓怕了。这样吧，请师父下马，找个背风的地方坐一坐，等我先去探望探望。’八戒打了个呵欠说：‘对，对，歇歇再走吧。’
3 好大圣，一纵身早到半空。向下一看，喝！悬岩边坐着个怪物，两旁站着一群小妖，在那里喷风吐雾哩。悟空暗想：‘我师父真的见识多了，连妖风邪气都能看出来了。’

[P4] 4 悟空原打算猛不防一棒捣死这个怪物，可又一想，明人不做暗事，我何不回去设法叫八戒来，先跟他见一仗，练练八戒的本领，也免得他整天偷懒。想罢，便落下云头。
5 唐僧见悟空回来忙问：‘是什么妖怪？’悟空道：‘不是妖怪，是村上许多善人，在那里斋僧施舍，几百口大锅，蒸馍煮饭，清油炒菜。蒸笼冒气，被山风一吹，所以显得迷迷蒙蒙的。’

[P5] 6 八戒一听早垂涎三尺，悄悄地拉过悟空问道：‘哥哥，你吃过了？’悟空说：‘吃了点儿，菜味太咸，油又太大，不喜欢多吃。’八戒说：‘啐！油大盐大才好吃哩，哥哥带我去吃一些吧！’
7 悟空看了看唐僧，八戒把嘴一撅做了个鬼脸说：‘只要哥哥不言语，师父好说。’悟空道：‘好，我不言语，看你怎么去说。’

[P6] 8 八戒嘿嘿嘿先笑了一阵，给师父行了个礼说：‘呆会儿我们要到前村化斋，我想去寻些嫩草，先把马喂饱，免得打搅人家。’唐僧说：‘好啊！难得你这样殷勤，快去快来！’
9 八戒拔腿就跑，悟空赶上扯住道：‘兄弟，人家可不斋丑和尚呀。’八戒说：‘那怕什么，咱会变呀。’说着变做个矮瘦和尚，手拿木鱼，不会念经，嘴里只哼着：‘白菜豆腐大米饭……’

[P7] 10 八戒正往前走，忽然被一群小妖围住，这个扯衣服，那个拉腰带，闹个不休。八戒只顾想吃喝，也没细看，便说：‘别推推拉拉的，等我一家一家的吃嘛！’
11 小妖道：‘你吃什么呀？我们正要把你拿到家里蒸熟吃哩！’八戒这才睁眼一看，暗骂猴头骗人。怎奈群妖扯住不放，急得八戒现了原形，举钯乱筑，吓得群妖乱叫乱跑。

[P8] 12 老妖出战，一看八戒那副长相，壮着胆子喝道：‘你是什么东西，快讲明白，饶你性命！’八戒笑道：‘我的儿，连你八戒爷爷都不认识，吃我一钯，给你开开窍吧！’
13 老妖一听喝道：‘原来你是唐僧的徒弟呀，我早想吃唐僧肉，正要找你们哩，休走看杵！’八戒笑道：‘我也认识你了，你是开染坊的吧。’老妖道：‘什么开染坊的？’八戒道：‘你不是开染坊的怎么会使棒槌呀！’

[P9] 14 那妖不容分说，把杵一抽，拦腰就扫，八戒忙用钯柄挡住，一翻手照头就盖，那妖举杵架起，杵来钯往，战得难解难分。
15 过了好大一阵，悟空不见八戒回来，便悄悄地对沙僧说：‘你在这陪伴师父，我去看看八戒。’说着拔根毫毛，小声叫‘变！’只见悟空一幌，假悟空仍站原处，真悟空早到空中去了。

[P10] 16 悟空在空中一看，八戒被群妖围住，扯手绊脚，乱戳乱打，弄得八戒不能还手。悟空忍不住按落云头，高声叫道：“八戒莫慌，老孙来了！
17 八戒听出悟空的声音，有了仗恃，挥动钉钯向前乱筑，吓得小妖四散。老妖道：“这笨猪先前不济，这会儿怎么又来后劲了？”八戒道：“我的儿，你别想欺负我，我家里的人来了！

[P11] 18 眼看八戒越战越勇，老妖节节败退。悟空便拨转云头，回到原处，把毫毛一抖，收上身来。沙僧笑了笑没言语。唐僧看了看悟空说：‘八戒去寻草，怎么还不回来？’
19 话音刚落，只见八戒累得气呼呼地回来了。唐僧忙问：‘八戒，你去寻草怎么连根蒿子也没拿来？还落得这般狼狈，是不是遇见看山的人，不容你打草呀？’

[P12] 20 八戒捶胸顿脚地说："师父呀，是我师兄拿白面馍馍捉弄我，我才假借打草为名，想弄些吃的。没想到遇上妖怪，不是师兄在空中助威，我老猪早被他们拿去蒸熟吃啦。"
21 悟空一旁笑道："这呆子做了贼，还拉别人入牢。我在这陪伴师父，一动也没动呀。"唐僧连连点头。八戒急得直嚷："师父，你别信他的，他拔根毫毛就是一个替身呀！"

[P13] 22 唐僧追问，悟空只得说了实话。叫过八戒过来吩咐道：‘你做个开路将军，打倒妖怪，算你的头功。’八戒与妖怪见过一仗，心里有底，并没推辞。于是唐僧上马，又继续上路了。
23 再说老妖回洞正为吃不到唐僧肉，闷闷不乐，有个小妖说道：‘我有个分瓣梅花计，保管捉到唐僧。’老妖听小妖细讲一遍，大喜道：‘妙计，妙计，事成之后一定封你做个前部先锋。’

[P14] 24 老妖照计行事。等了一会，唐僧到来，一个老妖从道旁跳出，拦住去路。八戒见了，连忙擎钯乱筑，那老妖用杵架住，且战且退，退到山坡后面去了。
25 悟空保护师父刚走不远，从草丛里又钻出一个老妖。悟空道：‘八戒真拙，怎么把妖怪放到这里来了。’说着举棒就打，那老妖也不答话，只战了几个回合，便把悟空引到山南去了。

[P15] 26 这时，从山后又来个老妖。沙僧见了大惊道：‘怎么大哥的眼也花了，让妖怪跑到这里来了。师父坐好，等我去拿他！’那妖见沙僧打来，马上向山北败退，沙僧不知是计，便赶到山北去了。
27 唐僧独坐马上，正在发愁，就听空中一阵笑声：‘唐僧呀唐僧，你的徒弟全是脓包，中了大王我的分瓣梅花计啦！’说罢，伸下五爪钢钩，把唐僧一把抓走了。

[P16] 28 老妖把唐僧拿到洞里，马上封那献计的小妖做了先锋，那小妖叩头谢恩，老妖得意地说：‘小子们，挑水刷锅，搬柴烧火，快蒸唐僧肉吃啊！’
29 先锋道：‘大王，唐僧的肉吃不得呀！’老妖把脸一沉说：‘怎么定计是你，不叫吃又是你呀！’先锋道：‘唐僧有个徒弟叫孙悟空，十分厉害，我以前在狮驼洞侍候的那个大王就是他打死的！’

[P17] 30 老妖听了，吃了一惊，忙问：‘先锋，依你的高见呢？’
先锋道：‘依着我，把他先绑在后园的树上，饿他三天，等
他的徒弟走了，再自自在在地受用。’老妖连连称赞他有见
识。
31 唐僧被绑在大树上，想起悟空他们不知道自己的下
落，难来搭救，不觉眼泪流下。忽听对面树上有人叫道：
‘长老，你也是被妖怪抓进来的？’

[P18] 32 唐僧忙问那人是干什么的？那人叹道：‘我是个打柴的樵夫，家里有老母，我死了谁照料她老人家。’唐僧也叹道：‘我是奉旨取经的，我死了怎报君恩？’两个人同命相怜，禁不住相对痛哭。
33 再说悟空战退老妖后，却又不知师父和沙僧哪里去了，急得他牵着白马，挑着行李，满山寻找，到处呼叫。

[P19] 34 忽见八戒跑来，悟空忙问：‘八戒，你见师父没有？’
八戒道：‘都是你捉弄我，偏偏遇上个妖怪是个属驴的，给我推磨打转转，累得我满身大汗。师父是你们看着，为啥问我？’
35 悟空道：‘原来是你赶不上妖精，所以妖精又跑回来了。我去打妖精，叫沙僧看着师父，现在连沙僧也不见了。’
八戒笑道：‘想是他们解手去了，我们坐下等等吧。’

[P20] 36 话刚说完，沙僧回来了。沙僧一讲刚才的情况，悟空气得暴跳起来：‘我们中了分瓣梅花计，妖精把我们调开，把师父劫走了。横竖就在这座山上，我们赶快去找吧！’
37 三人在这座大山上找来找去，才在悬崖下找到一座洞府，石门紧闭，门头石板上横写八个大字：隐雾山折岳连环洞。

[P21] 38 悟空道：‘这就是妖怪的住处，大家快动手！’八戒一钯下去，把石门筑了九个大窟窿，叫道：‘快把我师父放出来！要不，我再一钯就筑得门倒洞塌，把你们一家子全砸死在洞里！’
39 洞内小妖乱成一团，老妖大惊，先锋向外看了看说：‘大王别怕，这个是猪八戒，没大本事，他若无理，开了门，拿他进来一锅蒸了。怕只怕那个毛脸雷公嘴的孙悟空。’

[P22] 40 八戒在外面听见这话，向悟空道：‘哥呀！师父一定在里面，他们说不怕我，只怕你，你赶快上来打呀！’
41 悟空一阵叫骂，吓得老妖直埋怨先锋惹下大祸。先锋道：‘大王放心，那孙悟空别看神通广大，却是个宽宏大量的猴头。依我之见先送个木人头出去，就说把他师父吃了。哄过去就罢，哄不过去再想办法。’

[P23] 42 先锋命小妖把木人头包好，端到洞口叫道：‘大圣爷爷，息怒容禀，你师父被我大王拿进洞来，被那些不懂事的小妖，咬的咬，啃的啃，吃得只剩个头了。’说着便把头抛了出来。
43 八戒抱起人头就哭，悟空笑道：‘你的泪可真多呀，你也不辨个真假就哭。’八戒道：‘人头还有假的？’悟空道：‘你就不听听哪有人头落地登登响的，一定是个假的。’

[P24] 44 八戒不信。悟空用棒一敲，噗的一下，把人头打得粉碎，原来是个柳木疙瘩。
45 八戒大怒，正要叫骂，悟空道：‘别急，我看这妖怪诡计多端，等我混进洞去，你们再在洞外叫骂。我在洞里看他们耍什么花招。’

[P25] 46 悟空变了个小蚂蚁飞进洞去。八戒、沙僧在洞外高声叫骂，先锋听了忙说：‘好办，好办，他们认出是假的，就找个真的送出去，多说好话，他们便走开了。’老妖吩咐快办。
47 老妖还不放心，又命众妖搬石运土，把洞口堵死。这时，那个送头的小妖回来报道：‘好了，好了，那几个和尚抱住人头埋在山崖上正哭哩！’先锋得意地说：‘等他们走了，大王就可以吃唐僧肉了。’

[P26] 48 悟空在暗里听得明白，心内欢喜道：‘我师父还藏在洞里，并没吃掉，等我先去寻寻，看是死是活，再来收拾这伙妖魔。’
49 好大圣，‘嗡’的一声，飞出中堂在后园寻着唐僧，忍不住现了原相，上前轻轻地叫了一声：‘师父。’

[P27] 50 唐僧一见悟空，哭着说：‘你可来了，快快救我！’悟空连忙把师父解下来，说：‘你可不要动，等我去把那些妖怪收拾了，再来救你出去。’
51 悟空摇身又变个小飞蚂蚁，飞回中堂，见众妖正议论怎样吃唐僧肉呢。悟空拔撮毫毛，变作瞌睡虫儿，往众妖面上一撒，霎时鼾声如雷，连老妖也睡着了。

[P28] 52 悟空暗喜，现出本相，从耳朵里取出棒来，幌一幌，有鸭蛋粗细。“当”的一声，把旁门打破，跑到后园，扶着师父就走。
53 唐僧连忙拉住悟空，指指那樵夫道：“他也是被妖精捉来的，家里还有个八十岁的老母，快把他也救出去吧！”

[P29] 54 悟空忙替那人解开绳索。忽然想起洞门不通，马上回到中堂提来一个小妖，用冷水把小妖喷醒。小妖连呼饶命。悟空道：‘快引我们从后门出洞，饶你不死！’那小妖连称：‘是，是……’
55 悟空领着师父、樵夫，跟随小妖从后门出洞，去找八戒、沙僧。

[P30] 56 唐僧叫了声八戒，八戒吓了一跳，说：‘呀，沙僧你看，师父的头怎么还在脖子上呀！’悟空喝道：‘呆子！别胡说，快扶师父坐下歇歇，我还得收拾那伙妖怪去！’
57 悟空正往前走，只见众妖一拥而上，不觉一怔。原来是那送悟空出洞的小妖，回去用冷水把众妖喷醒。老妖和先锋领了小妖，杀出洞来了。

[P31] 58 悟空大战群妖，冲冲撞撞，真不耐烦。于是使个分身法，把毫毛拔下一把，嚼在口中，喷出去，叫声“变！”马上满山遍地都是悟空。
59 金箍棒好似万道电光，四个悟空围住一个小妖，手起棒落，几百个小妖一齐丧命。妖怪现了原形，都是些黄狼、狐狸、地老鼠之类。

[P32] 60 八戒见悟空打得热闹，吩咐沙僧保着师父，自己赶来助战。正好遇到先锋，八戒猛地照头一钯，那先锋不防，应钯倒地，八戒一看，原来是个铁背苍狼怪。
61 老怪一看兵丧将亡，正想逃走，早被悟空识破，悟空用手一挥，只见那群猴子手牵手、脚勾脚，结成天罗地网，把老妖困在中间。

[P33] 62 老妖东冲西撞，逃不掉。悟空上前就是一棒，打得老妖现了原形，原来却是一个艾叶花皮豹子精。
63 樵夫看了，又惊又喜，感激得热泪盈眶，说：‘就是这伙妖怪，害得我们这一带路断人稀，五谷不生。今天师父们除了此害，以后，我们可该过太平日子了！’

[P34] 64 唐僧吩咐收拾行装，继续上路。樵夫上前拦住说：
“请到我家见见家母，叩谢救命之恩。再备些粗茶淡饭，
将就吃些，休息一晚，明早再走。”
65 唐僧见樵夫诚心实意，只好答应。一进村，远远看见一个老妇，倚着门，正盼儿子归来。

[P35] 66 樵夫连忙跑到老妇跟前，跪下叫道：‘妈妈，儿回来了！’老妇一把抱住他道：‘儿呀，你再不回来，娘就要想死了……’
67 樵夫把山里的事对妈妈一讲，娘儿俩连忙把唐僧师徒迎到家中。老妇擦干眼泪，笑着说：‘救命恩人到了，怎奈山村寒舍，糙米野菜，将就吃些吧！’

[P36] 68 八戒忙说:“不管粗细，快些就好，俺可真饿了!”樵夫忙说:“就做，就做。”
69 唐僧师徒吃饱睡足，第二天一早，整装起程。老妇连夜赶做一些饽饽，送到村头，嘱咐樵夫道:“儿呀，你可要把恩人们送到上天竺国的大路再回来呀!”欲知后事，请看《悟空斗狮精》

[P1] Lian Huan Dong
The Thirty-First Story of Journey to the West
Original Author: Wu Cheng'en
Adapted by: Chen Pingfu
Illustrated by: Xuan Guanchao
Hebei Fine Arts Publishing House

[P2] Content Summary
This picture book is adapted from the classical literary masterpiece "Journey to the West," Chapters 85-86.
The story narrates how, on their journey to the West to obtain scriptures, Tang Sanzang and his disciples passed through the Lianhuan Cave of Yinfu Mountain, where Tang Sanzang was abducted by demons in the cave. Wukong displayed his divine power, eliminated the demon, the Aiye Huapi Leopard Spirit, rescued his master and a woodcutter, and allowed the people of Yinfu Mountain to return to peaceful lives.

1 The four disciples of Tang Sanzang, having left Xiankong Mountain, continued westward. After a few days, they encountered a high mountain blocking their path. At the foot of the mountain, suddenly a fierce wind raised dust and thick mist filled the sky. Tang Sanzang reined in his horse and cried out: "There's an ominous aura in this mountain! Why am I feeling numb all over, my heart trembling with fear!"

[P3] 2 Wukong smiled: 'Master is frightened by the demons. Here's what we'll do—please dismount, Master, and find a sheltered spot to rest while I go scout ahead.' Bajie yawned and said: 'Right, right, let's rest a bit before continuing.'
3 The Great Sage leaped into the air. Looking down, he exclaimed: 'Hey! By the cliffside sits a monster, flanked by a group of small demons, spewing wind and mist. Wukong thought to himself: 'My Master truly has keen insight—he can even spot demonic winds and evil auras.'

[P4] 4 Wukong originally planned to strike the monster unexpectedly with a single blow, but then thought, 'A straightforward person doesn't do underhanded things. Why not go back and find a way to call BaJie, have him face the monster first, practice his skills, and also prevent him from being lazy all day?' After thinking this, he descended from the clouds.
5 Tang僧 saw Wukong return and hurriedly asked, 'What kind of monster is it?' Wukong replied, 'It's not a monster. It's many kind people from the village, offering food to monks and guests. There are hundreds of big pots, steaming buns, cooking rice, frying vegetables with clear oil. The steam from the steamers, blown by the mountain wind, makes it look hazy and misty.'

[P5] 6 Pigsy, upon hearing this, immediately drooled, secretly pulled Sun Wukong aside and asked, 'Brother, have you eaten?' Wukong replied, 'I ate a little. The food was too salty and too oily; I didn't like eating much.' Pigsy said, 'Pfft! Food is only delicious when it's oily and salty. Brother, take me to eat some!' 
7 Wukong glanced at Master Tang. Pigsy pouted, made a funny face, and said, 'As long as you don't say anything, Brother, I can convince the Master.' Wukong replied, 'Alright, I won't say a word. Let's see how you'll manage to convince him.'

[P6] 8 Pigsy chuckled, bowed to his master, and said: 'In a bit, we'll go to the village ahead to beg for alms. I'd like to find some tender grass to feed the horse first, so as not to trouble the people.' The Master said: 'Good! It's rare for you to be so diligent. Go quickly!' 
9 Pigsy took off running, but Wukong caught up and pulled him back, saying: 'Brother, people won't give alms to ugly monks.' Pigsy replied: 'What's the problem? We can change!' Saying that, he transformed into a short, thin monk, holding a wooden fish, unable to chant scriptures, and humming in his mouth: 'Cabbage, tofu, rice...'

[P7] 10 Pigsy was walking forward when suddenly surrounded by a group of small demons. One pulled his clothes, another tugged his belt, and they made a fuss. Pigsy, only thinking about food and drink, didn't look closely and said, 'Stop pushing and pulling! Let me eat one family at a time!'
11 The small demons said, 'What are you eating? We're going to take you home and steam you to eat!' Pigsy then opened his eyes and secretly cursed the Monkey King for deceiving him. But the demons held him tight, and in desperation, Pigsy revealed his true form, swinging his rake wildly, scaring the demons into screaming and running away.

[P8] 12 The old demon came out to fight. Seeing Zhu Bajie's appearance, he plucked up his courage and shouted, 'What are you? Speak clearly, and I'll spare your life!' Bajie laughed, 'My boy, you don't even recognize Uncle Bajie. Take this shovel and let me open your eyes!'
13 The old demon shouted upon hearing this, 'So you're Tang Sanzang's disciple! I've long wanted to eat the flesh of Tang Sanzang. I was just looking for you. Don't run—wait for my staff!' Bajie laughed, 'I recognize you now. You must run a dye workshop, right?' The demon asked, 'What do you mean, a dye workshop?' Bajie replied, 'If you weren't running a dye workshop, how could you wield a mallet like that!'

[P9] 14 The demon didn't hesitate, pulled out his staff, and swept it horizontally at Zhu Bajie's waist. Bajie quickly blocked with the handle of his rake, then flipped his hand and swung it down at the demon's head. The demon raised his staff to block, and they clashed staff against rake, fighting fiercely and evenly.
15 After a long while, Wukong didn't see Bajie return. He quietly told Sha Wujing, 'You stay here with the Master, I'll go check on Bajie.' Saying this, he plucked a strand of hair and whispered, 'Transform!' In an instant, Wukong flickered, the fake Wukong remained standing in place, while the real Wukong had already soared into the sky.

[P10] 16 Wukong looked down from the sky and saw Bajie surrounded by a group of demons, tripped and tangled, being attacked wildly, leaving Bajie unable to fight back. Wukong couldn't bear it and landed from the clouds, shouting loudly: "Bajie, don't panic, I'm here!"
17 Bajie recognized Wukong's voice, gained confidence, swung his rake forward wildly, scaring the small demons away. The old demon said: "This clumsy pig was useless before, how come he's got a second wind now?" Bajie replied: "My boy, don't try to bully me, my family has come!"

[P11] 18 Seeing Bajie fighting with increasing bravery and the old demon retreating step by step, Wukong turned his cloud and returned to the original spot, shook his hair, and retracted his clone. Sha Wujing smiled silently without speaking. Tang Sanzang looked at Wukong and said, 'Bajie went to gather grass, why hasn't he returned yet?'
19 Just as he finished speaking, Bajie returned, exhausted and panting. Tang Sanzang hurriedly asked, 'Bajie, why didn't you bring even a single stalk of grass? You look so disheveled—did you meet the mountain guardian who wouldn't let you gather grass?'

[P12] 20 Pigsy pounded his chest and stomped his feet, saying: "Master, it was my elder brother who tricked me with white steamed buns. I only pretended to go for grass to get some food. I didn't expect to run into demons. If not for my brother's help from the sky, I would have been steamed and eaten long ago."
21 Wukong laughed beside him: "This fool committed theft and even dragged others into trouble. I've been staying with you, Master, not moving a bit." Tang Sanzang nodded repeatedly. Pigsy, frantic, shouted: "Master, don't believe him! He can create a clone with just one hair!"

[P13] 22 The monk pressed for an answer, and Wukong had to tell the truth. He called over Bajie and instructed him: 'You be the vanguard general, defeat the demons, and it will count as your top merit.' Bajie had faced the demons before and felt confident, so he didn't refuse. Then the monk mounted his horse and continued on the journey.
23 Meanwhile, the old demon returned to his cave, unhappy that he couldn't get the monk's flesh. A small demon said: 'I have a plan called the 'Split Plum Blossom Strategy' that will surely capture the monk.' The old demon listened to the small demon explain it in detail and exclaimed happily: 'Brilliant plan, brilliant plan! Once successful, I will definitely appoint you as the vanguard commander.'

[P14] 24 The old demon carried out the plan. After waiting for a while, Tang Sanzang arrived, and an old demon jumped out from the roadside, blocking the path. Bajie saw this and immediately swung his rake wildly. The old demon blocked with his staff, and they fought while retreating, eventually withdrawing behind a hill.
25 Wukong, having just protected his master a short distance, saw another old demon emerge from the grass. Wukong said, 'Bajie, you're really clumsy—how did you let the demon get here?' He then raised his staff and attacked. The old demon didn't respond, and after only a few rounds, he led Wukong southward.

[P15] 26 At this moment, another old demon came from behind the mountain. Sha Wujing was shocked and exclaimed: 'How could Big Brother's eyes be so blurry? He let the demon get this far. Master, stay put, I'll go get him!' The demon, seeing Sha Wujing charging, immediately retreated northward. Sha Wujing, unaware of the trick, chased after him to the north.
27 Master Tang sat alone on his horse, feeling anxious, when suddenly he heard a laugh from the sky: 'Master Tang, Master Tang, your disciples are all useless! You've fallen for King's Split Plum Blossom Strategy!' With that, the demon extended his five-clawed steel hook and grabbed Master Tang in one swift motion.

[P16] 28 The old demon took Tang Sanzang into the cave, immediately made the small demon who suggested the plan the vanguard, and the small demon bowed to show gratitude. The old demon proudly said: 'You guys, fetch water, scrub the pot, bring firewood, and quickly steam Tang Sanzang's meat to eat!'
29 The vanguard said: 'Your Majesty, Tang Sanzang's meat cannot be eaten!' The old demon frowned and said: 'You devised the plan, and now you're the one saying not to eat it!' The vanguard replied: 'Master Tang has a disciple named Sun Wukong, who is extremely powerful. The king I served before in the Shituo Cave was killed by him!'

[P17] 30 The old demon, upon hearing this, was startled and hurriedly asked: 'General, what's your advice?' 
The general replied: 'According to me, tie him first to a tree in the back garden, starve him for three days, wait until his disciples leave, then enjoy him at your leisure.' The old demon praised him repeatedly for his insight.
31 Tang Sanzang was tied to a big tree. Remembering that Wukong and the others didn't know his whereabouts and couldn't come to rescue him, he couldn't help shedding tears. Suddenly, he heard someone calling from the tree opposite: 'Elder, were you also captured by the demon?'

[P18] 32 Tang Sanzang hurriedly asked the man what he did. The man sighed, 'I'm a woodcutter with an old mother at home. Who will take care of her if I die?' Tang Sanzang also sighed, 'I am on a mission to fetch scriptures. How could I repay the Emperor's grace if I die?' The two, sharing similar fates, couldn't help but weep together.
33 Meanwhile, after Wukong drove back the old demon, he didn't know where his master and Sha Wujing had gone. In panic, he led the white horse, carried the luggage, and searched the mountains everywhere, calling out loudly.

[P19] 34 Suddenly, Pigsy ran over, and Wukong hurriedly asked: 'Pigsy, have you seen Master?'
Pigsy replied: 'It's all your fault for teasing me. I just happened to meet a demon who's a donkey, and he made me grind and spin around, exhausting me with sweat. The Master is your responsibility, why ask me?'
35 Wukong said: 'So you couldn't catch up with the demon, and that's why the demon came back. I went to fight the demon and told Sha Wujing to watch over the Master, but now even Sha Wujing is gone.'
Pigsy laughed: 'Probably they went to relieve themselves. Let's sit down and wait.'

[P20] 36 Just as he finished speaking, Sha Wujing returned. After Sha Wujing explained what had just happened, Wukong jumped up in anger: 'We fell for the divided plum-blossom trap! The demon separated us and kidnapped our master. He must be somewhere on this mountain—let's go find him quickly!'
37 The three searched up and down the mountain and finally found a cave府 at the base of a cliff. The stone door was tightly shut, and across the stone slab above the entrance were written eight large characters: 'Yinwu Mountain, Zheyue Lianhuan Cave.'

[P21] 38 Wukong said, 'This is the妖怪's dwelling, everyone, let's get to work!' Bajie swung his rake down, making nine big holes in the stone door, shouting, 'Quick, let my master out! Otherwise, with one more swing, I'll knock the door down and collapse the cave, crushing all of you inside!' 
39 Inside the cave, the little demons were in chaos, the old demon was greatly alarmed. The vanguard looked out and said, 'Your Majesty, don't be afraid. This is Zhu Bajie. He's not very capable. If he acts rashly, open the door and bring him in to be steamed in a pot. But we must be wary of that hairy-faced, thunder-god-mouthed Sun Wukong.'

[P22] 40 Pigsy, hearing this from outside, said to Wukong: 'Brother! Master must be inside. They say they're not afraid of me, but they're afraid of you. Hurry up and come fight them!'
41 Wukong started shouting and cursing, scaring the old demon who blamed the vanguard for causing a big disaster. The vanguard said: 'Your Majesty, don't worry. Although Sun Wukong is powerful, he's actually a generous and broad-minded monkey. In my opinion, let's send out a wooden head first, claiming we've eaten his master. If we can fool them, fine; if not, we'll think of another plan.'

[P23] 42 The vanguard ordered a small demon to wrap up the wooden head, carry it to the cave entrance, and shout: 'Great Sage, please calm down and listen. Your master was taken into the cave by our king, and was eaten by those irresponsible little demons—some bit, some gnawed, until only the head remained.' Then he threw the head out.
43 Pigsy picked up the head and started crying. Wukong laughed: 'You cry so much! You don't even distinguish real from fake before crying.' Pigsy asked: 'Can a head be fake?' Wukong replied: 'Don't you hear how it clatters when it hits the ground? It must be fake.'

[P24] 44 Pigsy didn't believe it. Wukong struck the head with his staff. With a 'puff,' the head shattered into pieces—it was just a willow wood lump.
45 Pigsy became furious and was about to shout insults. Wukong said, 'Don't rush. I see this demon is full of tricks. Let me sneak into the cave first, while you two shout outside. I'll see what tricks they have up their sleeves inside.'

[P25] 46 Wukong transformed into a tiny ant and flew into the cave. Bajie and Sha僧 were shouting loudly outside the cave. The vanguard, upon hearing this, hurriedly said: 'No problem, no problem. Since they've recognized the fake, just send out a real one, flatter them a bit, and they'll leave.' The old demon ordered them to act quickly.
47 The old demon was still not at ease, so he ordered the other demons to bring stones and soil to block the cave entrance. At that moment, the small demon who had delivered the head returned and reported: 'All done, all done! Those monks are holding the head and crying at the cliffside!' The vanguard said proudly: 'Once they leave, Your Majesty can eat the flesh of Tang Sanzang.'

[P26] 48 Wukong, having heard clearly in the dark, was delighted inside and thought: 'My master is still hidden in the cave and hasn't been eaten yet. Let me go search for him first, see if he's alive or dead, then I'll deal with these demons.'
49 The Great Sage, with a 'whoosh', flew out of the main hall and searched for Tang Sanzang in the back garden. Unable to hold back, he revealed his true form and gently called out, 'Master.'

[P27] 50 Tang Sanzang, upon seeing Wukong, cried out, 'You've finally come, quickly save me!' Wukong hurriedly untied his master and said, 'Don't move, I'll go take care of those demons first, then come back to rescue you.'
51 Wukong transformed again into a tiny flying ant, flew back to the central hall, and saw the demons discussing how to eat Tang Sanzang's flesh. Wukong plucked some hairs, turned them into sleepy bugs, and sprinkled them over the demons. Instantly, snoring echoed like thunder, even the old demon fell asleep.

[P28] 52 Wukong was secretly delighted, revealed his true form, took out his staff from his ear, waved it, and it became as thick as a duck egg. With a 'clang', he broke the side door, ran to the back garden, and helped his master leave.
53 Tang Sanzang hurriedly grabbed Wukong and pointed to the woodcutter, saying, 'He was also captured by the demon. He has an eighty-year-old mother at home. Quickly rescue him too!'

[P29] 54 Wukong hurriedly untied the ropes from the man. Suddenly remembering the front cave entrance was blocked, he quickly returned to the main hall, brought a small demon, and sprayed him with cold water to wake him up. The small demon cried out for mercy. Wukong said: 'Quickly lead us out of the cave through the back door, and I'll spare your life!' The small demon kept saying: 'Yes, yes...'
55 Wukong led the Master and the woodcutter, following the small demon out of the cave through the back door, to find Bajie and Sha Wujing.

[P30] 56 The monk called out to Eight戒, who jumped in fright and said, 'Hey, look, Sand Monk, the master's head is still on his neck!' Wukong shouted, 'Fool! Don't talk nonsense, quickly help the master sit down and rest, I still need to deal with those demons!' 
57 Wukong was walking forward when suddenly a group of demons rushed at him, making him startled. It turned out that the small demon who had sent Wukong out of the cave had returned and sprayed the other demons with cold water to wake them up. The old demon and the vanguard led the small demons out of the cave to attack.

[P31] 58 Wukong fought fiercely against the horde of demons, bumping and crashing, truly annoyed. So he used his body-splitting technique, plucked a handful of his fine hairs, chewed them in his mouth, spat them out, and shouted, 'Change!' Immediately, Wukong appeared everywhere across the mountains and fields.
59 The Golden Cudgel shone like countless flashes of lightning. Four Wukongs surrounded a small demon, and with a swing of the staff, hundreds of small demons perished at once. The demons revealed their true forms—nothing but yellow wolves, foxes, and mole rats.

[P32] 60 Pigsy saw Wukong fighting fiercely, and told Sha Wujing to protect the Master, then rushed to help. He met the vanguard, and with a sudden strike of his rake, the vanguard, unprepared, fell to the ground. Pigsy looked and saw it was an iron-backed gray wolf demon.
61 The old demon, seeing his troops defeated and generals fallen, tried to flee, but was already spotted by Wukong. Wukong waved his hand, and the monkeys linked hands and feet, forming a heavenly net, trapping the old demon in the center.

[P33] 62 The old demon dashed around frantically, unable to escape. Wukong stepped forward and struck him with a rod, forcing the demon to reveal his true form — it turned out to be a spotted leopard spirit.
63 The woodcutter looked on, both shocked and delighted, tears welling up in his eyes. He said, 'It was these demons who caused our region to become desolate, with no people and no crops. Now that you masters have eliminated this menace, we can finally live in peace!'

[P34] 64 The monk instructed them to pack up and continue their journey. The woodcutter stepped forward and said:
"Please come to my home to meet my mother and thank her for saving your life. I'll prepare some simple tea and food, eat a little, rest for the night, and leave early tomorrow."
65 The monk, seeing the woodcutter's sincere intentions, could only agree. As they entered the village, they saw an old woman leaning against the door, eagerly waiting for her son to return.

[P35] 66 The woodcutter hurried to his mother's side, knelt down, and called out: 'Mother, I'm back!' The old woman embraced him tightly and said: 'My child, if you hadn't returned, I would have died of longing...'
67 The woodcutter told his mother about the events in the mountains. The mother and son quickly welcomed Master Tang and his disciples into their home. The old woman wiped her tears and smiled: 'Our saviors have arrived! Though our mountain cottage is humble, and we have only coarse rice and wild vegetables, please eat some!'

[P36] 68 Pigsy hurriedly said, “Don’t mind if it’s coarse or fine, just hurry up—I’m really hungry!” The woodcutter quickly replied, “I’ll make it, I’ll make it.”
69 The Tang Monk and his disciples had eaten well and slept soundly. The next morning, they packed up and prepared to depart. The old woman had made some buns overnight and brought them to the village entrance, instructing the woodcutter, “My son, you must see your benefactors all the way to the main road leading to the Kingdom of Shangtianzhu before returning!” To learn what happens next, please read “Wukong Fights the Lion Demon.”

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为《西游记》连环画《连环洞》的封面，标明了故事名称、原著作者、改编者、绘画者及出版社信息。
[P2] 本页为《连环洞》故事的内容提要，介绍了画册改编自《西游记》第八十五回至八十六回，并简述了唐僧师徒在隐雾山连环洞遇险、孙悟空降妖救师的情节。下方第一幅图描绘了师徒四人行至高山脚下，唐僧因感到凶气而惊惧的场景。
[P3] 孙悟空见唐僧害怕，提议让他下马休息，自己前去探路；随后孙悟空腾云驾雾飞至半空，发现悬崖边有妖怪喷风吐雾，暗自感叹师父能察觉妖气。
[P4] 孙悟空本想直接打死妖怪，但转念决定叫八戒来练练本领，于是落下云头。唐僧见悟空回来，询问妖怪情况，悟空解释那并非妖怪，而是村民施舍斋饭，蒸煮食物产生的蒸汽被山风吹散所致。
[P5] 八戒听说有饭吃便垂涎三尺，向悟空打听并请求带他去吃；悟空答应不说话，让八戒自己去向师父说明。
[P6] 八戒向唐僧请求去寻草喂马，唐僧同意后，八戒立刻跑开，孙悟空追上阻止，提醒他人家不会给丑和尚施舍，八戒则自信能变装，随即化作矮瘦和尚，嘴里哼着想吃的饭菜。
[P7] 八戒被小妖围住，误以为是施舍斋饭，不以为意；小妖揭露要蒸吃他，八戒惊觉被骗，现出原形挥钯乱打，吓跑群妖。
[P8] 本页描绘了猪八戒与妖怪交战的场景。妖怪认出八戒是唐僧徒弟后欲吃其肉，八戒则以幽默方式嘲讽妖怪，称其使棒槌像开染坊的，场面充满戏剧性。
[P9] 本页描绘了猪八戒与妖怪激烈交战的场景，双方难分胜负；随后孙悟空因担心八戒安危，便化出分身，自己飞往空中查看情况。
[P10] 孙悟空在空中发现八戒被群妖围攻，无法还手，便降落云头高声呼救。八戒听到悟空声音后重拾信心，挥动钉耙反击，吓退小妖，并以幽默方式回应妖怪的嘲讽。
[P11] 孙悟空收起分身回到师父身边，唐僧询问八戒为何未归；话音刚落，八戒气喘吁吁地返回，唐僧责问他为何连草都没带回来，是否被看山人阻拦。
[P12] 八戒向唐僧诉说被妖怪围攻的经历，并归功于孙悟空的空中助威；孙悟空则笑着辩解自己并未离开师父身边，八戒急着澄清孙悟空能用毫毛变出替身。
[P13] 唐僧得知真相后，命猪八戒担任开路先锋，继续前行；与此同时，妖怪在洞中因未能捉到唐僧而懊恼，小妖献上‘分瓣梅花计’，老妖大喜并许诺事成后封其为先锋。
[P14] 本页描绘了妖怪按计策伏击唐僧师徒，猪八戒与老妖交战后退至山坡；随后孙悟空保护师父行进时，又遇一老妖，孙悟空出言责备八戒并与其交战，最终被引至山南。
[P15] 沙僧发现新出现的老妖，追击时中计；唐僧独坐马背发愁，被空中老妖用分瓣梅花计抓走。
[P16] 老妖将唐僧抓入洞中，封献计小妖为先锋，并下令准备蒸食唐僧肉。小妖却提醒老妖唐僧的徒弟孙悟空十分厉害，曾打死狮驼洞的大王，令老妖震惊。
[P17] 老妖采纳先锋建议，决定先将唐僧绑在后园树上饿三天再享用；唐僧被绑在树上，因担心徒弟不知其下落而落泪，此时听见对面树上有人询问他是否也被妖怪抓来。
[P18] 唐僧被绑在树上，与另一被捉的樵夫互诉身世，同命相怜而痛哭；孙悟空战退老妖后，因不知师父和沙僧下落，焦急地牵马挑担满山寻找并呼喊。
[P19] 孙悟空与猪八戒在山坡上相遇，孙悟空询问师父下落，猪八戒抱怨被妖怪戏弄并推卸责任；孙悟空得知沙僧也失踪后焦急，猪八戒则轻描淡写地认为他们只是去解手了。
[P20] 沙僧归来告知师父被妖怪用分瓣梅花计劫走，孙悟空愤怒并决定立即寻找；三人最终在悬崖下发现名为“隐雾山折岳连环洞”的洞府。
[P21] 孙悟空与猪八戒找到妖怪洞府，八戒用耙子砸门威逼放人；洞内妖怪惊慌，先锋判断来者是猪八戒，但担心孙悟空的厉害。
[P22] 孙悟空和猪八戒在洞外叫骂，猪八戒催促孙悟空进攻；洞内老妖惊慌，先锋建议用木人头骗过孙悟空以拖延时间。
[P23] 妖怪用木人头骗孙悟空，称唐僧已被吃剩头颅；孙悟空识破假头，指出落地有声必是假的。
[P24] 孙悟空识破妖怪用柳木疙瘩冒充唐僧头颅的骗局，随后决定独自潜入洞中探查妖怪的真正阴谋，而猪八戒和沙僧则在外接应叫骂。
[P25] 孙悟空化作小蚂蚁潜入洞中，猪八戒和沙僧在洞外叫骂；妖怪派小妖假扮唐僧头颅骗走悟空，老妖为防万一命众妖堵死洞口，并得知孙悟空等人已离开，得意地准备享用唐僧肉。
[P26] 孙悟空在洞中听到妖怪对话，确认师父未被吃掉，决定先去寻找；随后他化作小虫飞出，在后园找到被绑的唐僧，忍不住现出原形并轻声呼唤师父。
[P27] 孙悟空在后园找到被绑的唐僧并将其解救，随后化作小飞蚂蚁返回洞中，用瞌睡虫使众妖全部睡去。
[P28] 孙悟空现出原形，用金箍棒打破旁门，救出被绑的唐僧；唐僧随即请求孙悟空也救出被妖精捉来的樵夫，因其家中有八十岁老母。
[P29] 孙悟空救下被绑的樵夫，用冷水唤醒一个小妖，逼其带路从后门出洞，并带领唐僧和樵夫去找猪八戒与沙僧。
[P30] 孙悟空救出唐僧后，正带其离开，却被先前被他用瞌睡虫迷倒的小妖用冷水唤醒的众妖围攻，老妖和先锋率众杀出洞来。
[P31] 孙悟空与群妖激战，因敌众我寡而施展分身术，化出无数分身；随后四个孙悟空合力围杀小妖，众多妖怪现出黄狼、狐狸、地老鼠等原形被消灭。
[P32] 猪八戒赶来助战，用耙子击倒先锋妖怪；孙悟空识破老妖企图逃跑，指挥猴群结成天罗地网将其困住。
[P33] 孙悟空击毙老妖，使其现出艾叶花皮豹子精原形；樵夫目睹后感激涕零，称妖怪祸害当地，如今被除，百姓可过太平日子。
[P34] 唐僧一行准备上路，樵夫恳请他们到家中拜见母亲并休息一晚，唐僧答应后，进村时看到樵夫的老母亲正倚门盼子归来。
[P35] 樵夫与母亲团聚，激动相拥；随后母子二人将唐僧师徒迎入家中，老妇感激涕零，以粗茶淡饭款待救命恩人。
[P36] 唐僧师徒在樵夫家中休息一夜后，次日清晨整装出发。老妇人连夜做了饽饽送到村口，叮嘱儿子务必送师徒到上天竺国的大路再回来。
